scope_note: These source records support modeled housing scenario inputs. They do not identify a parcel-specific building design, meter, construction inventory, carbon footprint, or code-compliance result.

sources.title: Residential Prototype Building Models 2021 IECC - Climate Zone 5A
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Building Energy Codes Program; models developed by PNNL
sources.vintage: 2021 IECC; output tables generated 2024-06-27; DOE download page lists the dataset as published 2024-12-22
sources.geography: IECC 5A weather prototype uses Buffalo Niagara International Airport, NY TMY3; climate-zone representative only
sources.measurement_extract: For `US+SF/MF+CZ5A+hp+{foundation}+IECC_2021.table.htm`, use Electricity:Facility annual meter divided by Net Conditioned Building Area. Checked annual end-use fuel table: all non-electric energy carriers equal 0.
sources.relevant_details: DOE explains two residential base prototypes (single-family detached and multifamily low-rise), four heating systems, four foundations; each ZIP includes EnergyPlus IDFs and corresponding HTML output tables. HP-only outputs are used here without converting a gas-fired result.
sources.limitations: EnergyPlus prototypes are modeled reference buildings, not measured homes. Heat-pump all-electric scenario is an explicit scenario choice, not a claim that all local construction is all-electric. Buffalo weather, schedules, size, equipment, end uses and DOE model assumptions differ from Pittsburgh buildings. Foundation min/max is scenario sensitivity, not a statistical confidence interval.

sources.title: Embodied carbon benchmarks of single-family residential buildings in the United States
sources.authors: Matt A. Jungclaus, Nicholas Grant, Martín Torres, Jay H. Arehart, Wil V. Srubar III
sources.publication: Sustainable Cities and Society 117 (2024), article 105975; published 2024-12-15
sources.geography: Theoretical US DOE single-family detached prototype; 16 IECC climate zones and four foundation types; not Pittsburgh-specific.
sources.scope: Reported ECI uses A1-A3 product-stage LCA factors applied to modeled DOE single-family material quantities for structure, enclosure and foundation. This is not a complete all-systems whole-building, A1-A5 or whole-life inventory.
sources.source_extract: Abstract, reported results: “average ECIs ranged from 39 to 121 kgCO₂e/m².”

evidence_locations.extract: The paper reports average ECI values ranging from 39 to 121 kgCO2e/m2 across the prototype/tool cases.

evidence_locations.section: Methods: DOE single-family prototype model; material use intensity; life-cycle assessment
evidence_locations.extract: The study makes material quantity takeoffs for structure, enclosure and foundation, then applies product-stage A1-A3 factors from three LCA tools. It computes biogenic storage separately.

sources.use_in_lotline: Treat 39–121 kgCO2e/m2 as a published cross-model/tool range; convert to kgCO2e/sf. Center is the arithmetic midpoint, an explicit planning assumption, not a reported sample mean.
sources.biogenic_carbon: Use gross reported ECI; do not subtract the paper’s separately analyzed theoretical-maximum biogenic storage or assume that storage persists through end of life.
sources.limitations: The source benchmark covers detached single-family models only. Stated physical scope is structure, enclosure and foundation material classes; it does not establish that interior fit-out, MEP, appliances or site work are included. A1-A3 excludes installation-stage transport and construction (A4-A5), use/replacement and end-of-life stages. Multifamily/ADU/duplex/rowhouse values below are explicit typology proxies; wider proxy factors are scenario assumptions, not paper-reported intervals. Source range spans climate/foundation/modeling choices and is not a confidence interval.

reported_result.range_semantics: Published full study range across modeled DOE single-family prototypes, foundation/climate cases and the three LCA tools; not a statistical confidence interval.
reported_result.scope: A1-A3 product-stage, gross ECI for structure, enclosure and foundation material quantities.
